title.value: Recognizable series on graphs and hypergraphs
title.justification: The title of the paper is directly stated in the first page of the article, which provides a clear indication of the content being focused on recognizable series in the context of graphs and hypergraphs.
title.quote: Recognizable series on graphs and hypergraphs

analysis.description: This paper introduces the concept of Hypergraph Weighted Models (HWMs), which extends the notion of recognizable series from strings and trees to graphs and hypergraphs. The authors explore the algebraic properties of HWMs, focus on their application to non-classical graph families, and discuss the learnability of HWMs over circular strings. The study also considers closure properties and recognizability of finite support series within this new computational model.

type.justification: The paper develops a new computational model (HWMs) by theoretically extending the concept of recognizable series. It focuses on algebraic characterizations and properties, rather than empirical evaluation or application data.
type.quote: We introduce the notion of Hypergraph Weighted Model (HWM), a computational model... A series r defined on a hypergraph family is said to be recognizable if there exists a HWM that computes it.

is_compared.quote: We then investigate to what extent HWMs inherit fundamental properties that are satisfied by the classical notions of recognizable series on strings and trees.
